title: North Hall, University of Wisconsin (Wisconsin Historical Society property record HI100645)
notes: Round 9 (2026-10-29), owner feedback item 6 (North Hall room). Wisconsin Historical Society Architecture and History Inventory record for North Hall, 1050 Bascom Mall, Madison; the page states John Muir lived in the building 1861-1863. The legacy url https://www.wisconsinhistory.org/Records/Property/HI100645 answers 301 to a /redirect path; this is the page's own canonical link (rel=canonical), which answers 200.

claim: John Muir lived in North Hall at the University of Wisconsin.
place: North Hall, University of Wisconsin, Madison

evidence.quote:
February : Enrolls at the University of Wisconsin and attends for almost 2 1/2 years (5 trimesters); teaches school in winter
Learns about geology from Dr. Ezra S. Carr . Carr's wife, Jeanne, becomes his mentor
Invents a study desk that retrieves a book, holds it in place for the prescribed period of time, and then automatically replaces it with another book
Muir has his first informal lesson in botany from from Milton S. Griswold, a classmate, beneath a black locust near North Hall, the student residence hall where he was then living.
North Hall originally housed lecture rooms, a chapel, laboratories, a library, and dormitory rooms. Naturalist John Muir was its most famous student-resident, living here from 1861 to 1863
evidence.locator: property record, Additional Comments, first paragraph

evidence.quote: The first building erected by the University of Wisconsin was North Hall

notes: Round 9 (owner feedback item 6, 2026-10-29): corroborates MUI-F-0113 (single-source, Sierra Club only) with a second holder, the Wisconsin Historical Society property record for North Hall (HI100645). Worded with the words both holders share; no year is claimed (the WHS record says 1861 to 1863; the Sierra Club places it in its 1861 entry). The 1975 NHL nomination for North Hall (NPS 66000021) was read and does not name Muir.

claim: At the University of Wisconsin, Muir invented a study desk.

evidence.quote:
February : Enrolls at the University of Wisconsin and attends for almost 2 1/2 years (5 trimesters); teaches school in winter
Learns about geology from Dr. Ezra S. Carr . Carr's wife, Jeanne, becomes his mentor
Invents a study desk that retrieves a book, holds it in place for the prescribed period of time, and then automatically replaces it with another book

Clockwork study desk built by naturalist John Muir while at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, 1861-1863.

As a young man, however, Muir also invented and built numerous mechanical devices, including this magnificent clockwork desk, made between 1861 and 1863 while he was a student at the University of Wisconsin in Madison.

notes: Round 9 (owner feedback item 6): the verified tie between his inventions and his years at the University of Wisconsin (Madison) for the first-work chapter. Two holders: Sierra Club (1861 entry) and Wisconsin Historical Society article CS2641.

place: North Hall, University of Wisconsin, Madison
